title: TR-6 RX-124 WOUNDWORT GUNDAM
summary: A relic of a dead brand. It has only one product as I have researched and it is kind of interesting build. The mold seems broken at many places results in plenty of bit to be handled carefully. The design is quite good for a third party product with some questionable choices of pegs and holes. The final product however is looking amazing as it should. I love it despite all the faults.
body: A relic of a dead brand. It has only one product as I have researched and it is kind of interesting build. The mold seems broken at many places results in plenty of bit to be handled carefully. The design is quite good for a third party product with some questionable choices of pegs and holes. The final product however is looking amazing as it should. I love it despite all the faults.

If only this kit design were done by Bandai, the kit could have been an excellent MG of its own. Or if CuteCube lived long enough to earn more experience, they might be a outstanding player in the field of model kit makers. Don't touch this if you have low tolerant or high standards, this is a fun experiment but it could be frustrating.
✔ Has cockpit, although the hatch is difficult to open
✔ Look better than "just an oversized HG"
❌ Difficult to replace the hands without ripping the joint off then putting it back again
Honorable mention: Tamiya Extra Thin Cement. It keeps the kit together pretty well and should be your best friend.
Artwork used in video is from https://www.deviantart.com/krisoyo
